draft_evidence.quote: The eleventh had been a plane held across a cut for him, and he had told the man on a step, in the only currency the man took, which was a ledger.

comparison_evidence.quote: Then he said, "It's entered," and took the log out, on the step, and wrote it, and did not tell the man what else he had entered, because a fragment is a thing you own and a thing a man gave you is a thing you owe, and he did not yet have a word for the distance between those two, and was not going to make one up on a step.

findings.consequence: Chapter 12 closes on Cael deliberately NOT telling Vastin about the eleventh fragment — it is the chapter's last withheld thing and a live open thread. findings.consequence: Counted over the whole draft: 'six days' appears six times (ll.15, 25, 45, 65, and twice at 69) and the 'as a man/woman [verb]' simile engine six times (l.31 'as a man's breath changes'; l.37 'as a man looks at somebody'; l.53 'as a man holds a thing'; l.77 'as a man looks at the thing'; l.87 'as a woman's hand coming off a page'; l.91 'as a man nods who has spent forty years'). concerns: Word count sits 41 words above the floor (3,951 against a 3,910 minimum). Every repair that cuts — CH13-002's interpolations, CH13-009's tic reductions, CH13-014's duplicated gesture — pushes the chapter under band. The repair pass should plan an expansion alongside the cuts; the obvious candidate is the eye-cost (below).

The notice promises a cost — 'Costs the eyes, after' (l.95) — that the chapter never pays. Cleon's version costs him his eyes for an hour (Ch11 l.39); Cael renders the notice on a stair and then reads a log by lamplight and climbs to the tiers with no eye trouble at all. The involuntary leaning at l.53 is a fine consequence but it is not the cost the notice names. Charter §6.2 wants every rule to visibly cost; this is the place to spend the words the repair frees.

The handcart at l.3 ('a broker's handcart that Seln had borrowed for a copper and a look') is introduced as the route's new fact and then disappears. At the bell Cael 'picked up the box' and carries it up the stair by hand (ll.107-109) with no cart at the yard door. DECISION row 16's staging is the crew carrying boxes; a wheeled substitute appearing for one line and vanishing is a loose prop, and Ch14/Ch16/Ch17 will have to decide whether it is still borrowed.

'six days' as the lamp count (ll.25, 69) is defensible against Cleon's week (packet: 'Cleon's week is at its sixth day'), but Vastin's 'six days of watching Cael' (l.15) and the lamp-reach tally 'four, on the fourth day; two, today' (l.53) index off Vastin's own tenure, and Vastin came down as a hand on the 284th (Ch9's four hands) — the 291st is his eighth day. Worth one pass to put every count on the same clock.

Vastin's 'You told him' and 'He looked away' (l.91) name two things he did not see: he took the case and went up before the telling (l.63). The narration's gloss ('a man nods who has spent forty years watching people be told things') carries it as a professional's read, and I am not raising it — but if the repair touches l.91 for CH13-010 anyway, one clause of inference framing would close the gap for free.

l.31's 'for the length of the reading' is a structural cousin of 'for the length of a breath', which is capped at zero for this chapter and which Ch12 used (ch12.md l.71). Not a breach; flagged so the phrase does not become the book's next watermark.

Ten sentences run over 90 words, four over 110. The median is 7.5, so the contrast the charter asks for is genuinely there and the accumulation is house voice doing real work at ll.11, 15 and 53. Only l.91 crosses into a defect (CH13-010); the rest is taste and I am leaving it.
strengths: The inside/outside distinction is the best piece of Path-craft exposition the book has produced. 'A record sits ... An instruction *leans*' (l.27) gives the reader a physical test they can apply themselves, and the stair image ('you can feel the order as you can feel which way a stair goes in the dark by where the treads are') pays off twice — at l.33 'This is a stair' and at l.91 in the actual stair. Do not sand this.

The acquisition is staged through the wrong sense on purpose and it works: Cleon's eyes do NOT move, and it is the attention that travels, and Cael can only know it went because the man's breath changes at each bearer (l.31). Integration by observation has never been this legible or this cheap to believe.

'He knew the moment this time' (l.43) and the paragraph that follows — the row leaning 'Not much. The way a floor leans that you have stood on for an hour before you notice it is not quite level' — is the strongest rendering of an integration in the series so far, because it refuses to make the new sense useful.

Karis's beat at l.37 is the chapter's quiet victory: she is given a finding of her own out of Cleon's demonstration ('The strata lean too ... I thought that was weight'), and Cleon answers with one word because 'a thing said by somebody else does not need saying twice'. She is not an audience for Cael's chapter.

The refusal at l.49 — he has the instrument, he has the one question he has wanted answered for five years, and he does not ask it — is the moral spine of the chapter and it is carried entirely by procedure. Preserve it verbatim through any repair.
Cleon's 'No. I'll not say that one. Not down here. Not to you.' (l.85) makes the unsaid sentence land harder than saying it would. The refusal is characterised, not withheld by the author.

l.97's reading of the look-away as 'the covenant's other half' — a man keeping the boy by declining to see him — earns the ending's ethics without a speech about them. (CH13-014 asks only that the gesture be performed once, not that this gloss be cut.)

The clerk's arithmetic of not-asking (ll.9, 11) — three things not asked, and 'a man who has not asked three things has a fourth in him somewhere' — is institutional pressure rendered as a count, which is exactly this book's method.
